sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know reported speech from B1 Unit 13: *dijo que*, *escribió que*, and the shift of tenses after a past verb. It is the tool for a debate in history: what the defenders of Rosas said, what Sarmiento wrote, what historians say today. Here we only report ideas, we do not quote them.

sections.title: Reporting with que
rows: Los defensores decían que Rosas mantenía el orden.
Sarmiento escribió que el campo representaba la barbarie.
*escribió que* + imperfect: what he wrote (the verb moves back in time)
Muchos historiadores dicen que la idea es simple.
a present verb (*dicen*) keeps the present: *es*

items.spanish: Los defensores de Rosas decían que él mantenía el orden.
items.english: The defenders of Rosas said that he kept order.

items.spanish: Sarmiento escribió que las ciudades representaban la civilización.
items.english: Sarmiento wrote that the cities represented civilization.

items.spanish: Escribió que los caudillos eran un obstáculo para el progreso.
items.english: He wrote that the caudillos were an obstacle to progress.

items.spanish: Muchos historiadores dicen que cada caso necesita su explicación.
items.english: Many historians say that each case needs its own explanation.

sections.content: After a past verb (*escribió que*, *decían que*) the verb of the report moves back: *mantiene* becomes *mantenía*, *son* becomes *eran*. After a present verb (*dicen que*) nothing changes. Never drop *que*: *escribió que el campo…*.
